items.guidance: Enumerate the s6-overlay service definitions referenced by the Dockerfile (oneshot init-* entries like init-folders and init-env-file are setup steps, not long-running programs) and separate them from long-running ones such as the web server, celery worker, celery beat, and any consumer. Any bundled Redis service needs no worker because Deployz provides Valkey; report it instead.

Check whether the app's settings already offer an S3 storage backend selectable by environment variable; if so, report those variable names and change no code. Treat any search index or cache under /usr/src/paperless/data as rebuildable and report it separately from persistent document data. Also check whether media or consume directories outside the declared VOLUME hold originals, and include them in the classification.

psycopg indicates a Python/Django backend, so check whether the runtime image contains manage.py and Django migration files, and whether an s6 init step already runs migrations at startup. Confirm whether the Prisma evidence applies to a component present in the runtime stage, and report it as not runnable if that stage lacks node_modules.

Locate the Celery app definition and the s6 service scripts that launch the celery worker and beat, and report their exact commands. If the scheduler runs as a separate process, report it as its own worker command rather than combining it with the worker. Confirm that the broker setting can read REDIS_URL or a variable the app already uses.
